_comment: Series config for the 'Why men...' flow. Read by scripts/generate_script_niche.py; the 'video' block is also passed to assemble_video.py --config. Add/remove topics freely.
channel_description: short psychology videos explaining why men think, feel and behave the way they do, told with empathy and respect for everyone
tone: calm, direct, second-person, quietly powerful; speaks to men who feel understood and to people who love them
footage_hint: filmable stock scenes: a man alone by a window at dusk, a man working late, silhouette on a rooftop, hands on a steering wheel, a father with a child, a man walking city streets at night, gym or workshop, a man looking at the horizon

skit._comment: Cartoon-skit format (format: skit). A recurring cast with name caps acts out each topic as a short dialogue scene; the narrator (the channel owner's cloned voice) closes with the psychology insight. Character sheets and location plates are generated once and cached in assets/skit/men_psychology/, so the cast looks the same in every video.

examples.topic: Why men rarely buy things for themselves
examples.title: NINE YEARS WITHOUT A NEW COAT
examples.narration: Daniel hasn't bought himself a coat in nine years. Picture him. Forty-one, two kids, a job he never mentions. Every payday, the money leaves in the same order. Rent. School shoes. Her birthday. His name is always last. Not because he doesn't want things. Because somewhere along the way, spending on himself started to feel like stealing from them. That's the quiet trap. When a man's worth is tied to what he provides, every purchase for himself feels like a loss. So he waits. Send this to the Daniel in your life.

examples.topic: Why men go silent when they are hurting
examples.title: WATCH WHAT A HURTING MAN DOES
examples.narration: Watch what a man does when he's hurting. Nothing. No call, no text, no scene. People call that cold. It isn't. Picture Marcus on the day he lost his job. He came home, kissed his wife, checked the kids' homework. Then he sat in the car for an hour. Here's why. Many men learned early that pain is something you solve alone, quietly, before anyone sees it. Silence isn't the absence of feeling. It's the feeling with the volume turned down. So if he goes quiet, skip the questions. Just sit beside him.
